The gas lamps, though guttered from wind, cast long wavering shadows over shuttered storefronts—Tallow’s Trap & Leather with its cracked glass and a warped wooden sign, the blacksmith’s forge glowing faintly orange below its sooty chimney. A low gust rattles the lanterns, scattering sparks into the alley behind the Griffin, where a cart wheel clatters against wood. The stink of hot iron and leather mixes with the acrid tang of pipe tobacco, thick enough to make the breath tighten. No one hurries, but no one lingers either—not in this town where the dusk comes early. The air cools further as a woman’s voice calls out from a doorway, muffled but sharp, about a lost mare.
